title: Introduce Prefill Sculptor: tenant-aware prefill orchestration and quant presets
author: Ariana Chen
description: Context and motivation: Tenant traffic warming (prefill) is an important lever for reducing per-token unit economics on cold-key workloads, but existing defaults are conservative, disconnected from observed tenant arrival curves, and require manual tuning. This PR adds a new runtime component (Prefill Sculptor) plus a lightweight CLI and config schema to automatically derive tenant-aware prefill policies and matching quantization presets. The goal is to provide safe, conservative defaults that drive measurable cost reduction while preserving latency SLOs and output quality. Summary of changes: 1) New prefill-sculptor service that subscribes to the metrics pipeline and synthesizes per-tenant prefill budgets and batch-shape hints; 2) Unit-econ simulator harness used to evaluate candidate presets offline against sampled traffic; 3) Compact quantization profile templates that map to runtime fallback tiers (float32, int8-q4, int4-stat); 4) CLI command (redwoodctl econ profile generate) to preview and dry-run derived defaults; 5) New telemetry signals and dashboards (prefill.hit_rate, prefill.eviction_rate, econ.estimated_cost_delta) and an Ops playbook for safe rollouts; 6) Conservative safety gates and automatic rollback based on quality regressions. Design notes: Prefill Sculptor uses a 2-phase approach: (A) Observe: sampling of tenant arrival distributions and recent prefix cache hit rates (1 minute windows); (B) Propose: run unit-econ simulation across a small grid of batch sizes, prefill budgets and quant presets to pick the Pareto-optimal candidate under a latency SLO constraint. The component is intentionally modular and can be run as a batch job or as a low-CPU long-running service. Rollout strategy: defaults are introduced behind a feature flag and are enabled as a canary for a small tenant subset, with automatic throttles and a manual opt-out. Backwards compatibility: existing config keys are unaffected; new defaults only apply when tenants adopt the schema or accept generated profiles via the CLI. Related work: builds on the economizer telemetry signals from ENG-7622 and the quant presets framework from ENG-7999.

release_notes: Adds a new opt-in Prefill Sculptor service that can generate tenant-aware prefill policies and quant presets. Includes a dry-run CLI and telemetry for safe rollouts. Default profiles are conservative; enable via feature flag. See docs/operators/prefill-sculptor.md for migration steps.
observability_changes: New metrics: prefill.hit_rate, prefill.eviction_rate, econ.estimated_cost_delta. Dashboard added: Prefill Sculptor - Unit Econ. Alerts: prefill.hit_rate < 0.2 for 5m; econ.estimated_cost_delta > +10%.
notes_for_release_engineering: Deployment: chart update included (charts/redwood-helm/prefill-sculptor-values.yaml). Rollout plan: 1) Deploy service as disabled by default; 2) Enable for internal canary tenant group; 3) Monitor prefill.hit_rate and econ.estimated_cost_delta for 24h; 4) Gradually expand. If quality regressions observed, set feature flag to 'off' to rollback.
impact_summary: Expected unit economics improvement: 3-8% cost-per-token reduction on cold-keyed tenants in simulated workloads; projected higher for workloads with high prefix reuse. Latency impact: within existing SLO for the tested presets; guardrails prevent aggressive quant transitions for latency-critical tiers.
test_plan_summary: Included tests: unit tests for sim harness, integration test that runs the CLI dry-run against a recorded trace, e2e smoke that validates metrics emission and feature-flag toggling. Manual test: ops-run checklist in ops/playbooks/prefill-rollout.md.
